findings.title: No API Interface — Direct Database Access Only
findings.description: The application is a VB6 Win32 desktop EXE that connects directly to a Microsoft Access .mdb file on an SMB file share. No REST, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or any programmatic interface exists. Integration requires direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No API exists. The only integration path is direct database manipulation or RPA-style UI automation — brittle, non-auditable, and unscalable.
findings.recommendation: Design and implement a REST API layer wrapping customer CRUD operations with an OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: No Idempotency Controls on Write Operations
findings.description: The only write operation (INSERT INTO Customers) uses no idempotency keys, no unique constraints, and no deduplication logic. String concatenation builds SQL directly from user input.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism exists. Agent retries would create duplicate customer records.
findings.recommendation: Implement idempotency key support and unique constraints on business keys in write operations.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No authentication mechanism exists. User identity is derived from Windows Environ("USERNAME") environment variable. No OAuth, API keys, mTLS, or service accounts.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. Agents cannot authenticate to this system and no principal attribution is possible.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth 2.0 client credentials or API key authentication with principal attribution.

findings.title: Zero Audit Logging
findings.description: The application has no logging whatsoever. Write operations execute with On Error Resume Next which swallows all errors silently. No CloudTrail, no application logs, no immutable storage.
findings.gap: Zero audit logging. No way to determine what operations were performed, by whom, or when.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging for all write operations with principal attribution and immutable log storage.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Unscoped — Direct Database Access
findings.description: Stage A: System stores customer PII (names). Stage B: B1 — no API response scoping (direct database access exposes all fields), B2 — no access control differentiation (single hardcoded password grants full access), B3 — no classification metadata.
findings.gap: Direct database access with no field filtering, no access differentiation, no classification controls.
findings.recommendation: Design API responses that exclude sensitive fields. Implement differentiated access scopes.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls for Customer PII
findings.description: Customer PII (names) stored with no residency controls, no documented requirements, and no mechanism to prevent cross-jurisdiction data transmission to LLM endpoints.
findings.gap: No data residency configuration. No compliance references. No cross-boundary transmission controls.
findings.recommendation: Document applicable data residency requirements and implement transmission controls.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: No compensation or rollback logic exists. INSERT executes with On Error Resume Next. No transactions, no undo, no compensation endpoints.
findings.gap: Failed multi-step agent workflows would leave inconsistent state with no recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Implement transaction boundaries and compensation/undo logic for write operations.

findings.title: No Programmatic API — HTML Pages Only
findings.description: The application exposes only HTML-rendered ColdFusion pages (index.cfm, download.cfm) served by IIS. There is no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration requires UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No programmatic API exists. The only integration surface is HTML pages rendered by ColdFusion 8.
findings.recommendation: Build a REST API with JSON responses exposing document search and download functionality.

findings.title: No Idempotency Controls on Write Operations
findings.description: Write operations (file uploads) have no idempotency keys, no unique constraints on business keys, and no deduplication logic.
findings.gap: Agent retries or duplicate calls would create duplicate records/files.
findings.recommendation: Implement idempotency key support for all write operations.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application supports only session-based human authentication. No OAuth2 client credentials, API key authentication, mTLS, or service accounts exist.
findings.gap: Agents cannot authenticate without human credentials.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind exists. No CloudTrail, no application-level audit trail, no immutable log storage.
findings.gap: Cannot determine who accessed or modified documents. Zero accountability trail.
findings.recommendation: Enable CloudTrail and implement application audit logging with immutable storage (S3 Object Lock).

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Logic
findings.description: No compensation or rollback logic exists. No saga patterns, undo endpoints, or compensating transactions. Writes commit immediately with no reversal mechanism.
findings.gap: Failed multi-step operations leave partial state with no recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Implement two-phase commit pattern with compensation logic for write operations.

findings.title: No Machine-Consumable API Interface
findings.description: The application exposes only HTML-rendered views via Django render_to_response and raw HttpResponse with HTML content. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Integration requires direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No machine-consumable API exists. Only HTML pages designed for human browsers.
findings.recommendation: Implement REST API layer with Django REST Framework after upgrading Python and Django to supported versions.

findings.title: No Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: No idempotency patterns exist. No idempotency keys, no unique constraint enforcement, no deduplication logic. Agent retries would create duplicate tickets.
findings.gap: Write operations have no idempotency guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Add idempotency key support to all write endpoints once REST API is implemented.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Only Django session-based authentication exists, designed for human browser sessions. No OAuth2 client credentials, no API key authentication, no mTLS, no service account support.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. Agents cannot authenticate without human credentials.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key or OAuth2 client credentials authentication with principal attribution in logs.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. No CloudTrail, no application-level audit trail, no log of authenticated principals for write operations. Only a print statement logging search queries without auth context.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail. Cannot prove who performed any action.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging capturing principal, action, resource, and timestamp for all write operations with immutable storage.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposed Without Scoping
findings.description: System stores employee data (requester field). B1: All fields returned without filtering in ticket_list and ticket_search views. B2: No access control differentiation. B3: No classification metadata.
findings.gap: Agent-facing responses would expose all fields indiscriminately. No mechanism to scope sensitive fields per caller.
findings.recommendation: Implement response serializers excluding sensitive fields from agent-facing API responses. Add role-based field visibility.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: Employee helpdesk tickets containing employee names and internal information stored with no residency controls, no region configuration, no sovereignty policies.
findings.gap: No data residency controls. Employee PII has no protection against cross-region transmission to LLM providers.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Configure same-region LLM endpoints. Implement technical controls preventing cross-region data transmission.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback patterns exist. No saga pattern, no two-phase commit, no undo endpoints. Raw SQL with no transaction management beyond Django autocommit.
findings.gap: Multi-step operations that fail mid-sequence leave partial state with no recovery.
findings.recommendation: Wrap multi-step operations in database transactions with compensation endpoints for business-level rollback.

findings.title: No programmatic API — legacy form-based web UI only
findings.description: The application is a legacy Struts 1.3 web application that exposes only a form-based HTML interface via JSP pages. There is no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration would require direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No programmatic API exists. The only integration surface is an HTML form-based Struts action mapped in struts-config.xml.
findings.recommendation: Expose the loan pricing calculation and submission as a REST API (e.g., Spring Boot with @RestController) alongside or replacing the Struts UI layer.

findings.title: Write operations are not idempotent
findings.description: The loan submission endpoint performs a raw INSERT into the applications table with no idempotency protection. No idempotency key, no unique constraint on business keys, no duplicate detection. Repeated submissions create duplicate loan applications.
findings.gap: No idempotency key support. No unique constraint enforcement. The saveApplication method performs unconditional INSERT on every call.
findings.recommendation: Add an idempotency key parameter to the submission endpoint. Enforce a unique constraint on a business key.

findings.title: No machine identity authentication mechanism
findings.description: The application has no machine identity authentication mechanism. It relies solely on container-managed authentication (request.getRemoteUser()) which provides no support for service accounts, API keys, OAuth2 client credentials, or mTLS.
findings.gap: No machine identity mechanism. No API key, OAuth2 client credentials, or mTLS configuration.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key or OAuth2 client credentials authentication on any new API surface. Use AWS Cognito or API Gateway authorizers for machine identity.

findings.title: No audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No audit logging exists. The application has no logging of any kind. Write operations (loan submissions) are not logged with the authenticated principal. No immutable log storage.
findings.gap: No audit trail for write operations. No CloudTrail. No log immutability.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging (CloudTrail + S3 Object Lock) capturing principal for every write operation.

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for loan submissions
findings.description: The application performs a single INSERT operation with no compensation, rollback, or saga pattern. No mechanism to undo a submitted loan application.
findings.gap: No rollback or compensation mechanism. No undo endpoint. No status field for cancellation.
findings.recommendation: Add a status field (PENDING, SUBMITTED, CANCELLED) and expose a cancellation endpoint.

findings.title: No modern API interface — SOAP-only endpoint
findings.description: The service exposes a SOAP 1.1 RPC/encoded endpoint via JAX-WS. The WSDL is hand-maintained and drifts from implementation. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Modern agent frameworks cannot bind to SOAP natively.
findings.gap: No REST or modern API interface. SOAP RPC/encoded is deprecated. Agent tool frameworks cannot consume WSDL/SOAP natively.
findings.recommendation: Expose submitOrder as a REST POST endpoint with JSON request/response. Generate OpenAPI spec. Deprecate SOAP endpoint.

findings.title: Write operations are not idempotent
findings.description: The submitOrder operation performs an unconditional INSERT with no idempotency key, no duplicate detection, and no unique constraint. Duplicate submissions create duplicate records.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism. No unique constraints on business keys. Retry creates duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add UNIQUE constraint on (partner_id, po_number) and implement idempotency key support in the API contract.

findings.title: No machine identity authentication
findings.description: No authentication mechanism exists in the source code. README mentions WS-Security but no implementation is committed. Any caller with network access can invoke the endpoint without authentication.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. No principal attribution. Service is completely unauthenticated.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials flow or API key authentication with distinct agent identities and principal attribution in audit logs.

findings.title: No audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No logging of any kind exists. No logging framework imported. Write operations leave no trace of who performed them. Complete absence of audit capability.
findings.gap: Zero audit logging. No logging framework. Impossible to identify who performed what action.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging with caller identity on every write. Deploy to immutable store (CloudWatch with retention or S3 with Object Lock).

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for write operations
findings.description: The submitOrder operation performs a single INSERT with no transaction management, no rollback capability, and no compensation logic. Submitted orders cannot be reversed programmatically.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback. No cancel/void endpoint. No transaction management.
findings.recommendation: Add database transaction management and a cancelOrder endpoint. Implement saga-pattern compensation with status-based order lifecycle.

findings.title: No API Interface — File-Based Integration Only
findings.description: The system exposes no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration requires file-based exchange: COBOL batch reads indexed employee master files and writes fixed-width flat files transferred via plaintext FTP to an EC2 gateway.
findings.gap: No API exists. Only file-based integration via plaintext FTP — brittle, non-auditable, non-programmatic coupling.
findings.recommendation: Build a REST API wrapper with OpenAPI specification exposing payroll operations (submit run, query status, retrieve results).

findings.title: No Idempotency Protection on Write Operations
findings.description: The batch payroll job has no idempotency protection. Duplicate execution produces duplicate payout records with no deduplication logic or unique constraint enforcement.
findings.gap: No idempotency keys, no deduplication logic, no duplicate-run detection.
findings.recommendation: Add pay-period identifier and duplicate-run detection before processing.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. Only a hardcoded FTP username/password (payroll/PayR0ll2003!) in the JCL — no OAuth2, no API keys, no mTLS, no principal attribution.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. Agent cannot authenticate with a distinct, attributable identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement service accounts with OAuth2 client credentials on modernized API.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. No CloudTrail, no immutable log storage, no principal attribution on write operations. SYSOUT is transient with no retention policy.
findings.gap: Zero audit trail. No immutable logging. No principal attribution.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logs (CloudTrail) with principal attribution for every operation.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposed Without Scoping
findings.description: System processes SSN (EMP-SSN) and bank account numbers (EMP-ACCT) with no output filtering. All sensitive fields are written to payout file and transmitted via plaintext FTP. No access control differentiation. No formal classification.
findings.gap: B1: Sensitive data in all output without filtering. B2: No access control differentiation. B3: No classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement field-level output filtering. Tokenize sensitive identifiers. Separate access controls for sensitive data.

findings.title: Data Residency Violation — Plaintext PII Transfer
findings.description: US-regulated PII (SSN) transmitted via plaintext FTP from mainframe to EC2 gateway with no encryption, no region controls, no residency configuration.
findings.gap: No data residency controls. No encryption in transit. PII crosses boundaries unprotected.
findings.recommendation: Replace plaintext FTP with encrypted transfer. Document and enforce data residency requirements.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: No compensation or rollback. Once the job writes payout records and FTPs the file, there is no undo. Partial failure leaves inconsistent state.
findings.gap: No saga, no compensating transactions, no undo endpoints, no rollback states.
findings.recommendation: Implement two-phase execution with explicit commit step and compensation logic.

findings.title: No Structured API Interface — HTML-Only CGI Response
findings.description: The application exposes an HTTP CGI endpoint at GET /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi that returns unstructured HTML. Integration requires HTML parsing — functionally UI automation. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists.
findings.gap: No structured API interface. HTML-only response requires parsing to extract pricing data. No machine-parseable output format.
findings.recommendation: Add JSON response mode by detecting Accept: application/json header or format=json query parameter. Return structured JSON with proper HTTP status codes.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application has zero authentication. Any network-reachable client can call the CGI endpoint without presenting credentials. No OAuth2, API key validation, mTLS, or service account mechanism exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. Agent cannot be distinguished from any other caller. No principal attribution.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with API key authentication and principal attribution. Alternatively, implement OAuth2 client credentials flow.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses a single static shared API key ('ship-2013-abc123-static') hardcoded in server.js. All callers share the same key. There is no per-principal attribution — the system cannot distinguish which agent or service made a request.
findings.gap: No machine identity mechanism with principal attribution. A generic shared API key with no caller differentiation is insufficient for audit and forensics.
findings.recommendation: Replace the shared static API key with per-caller API keys issued through AWS API Gateway or a centralized identity provider (Cognito app clients with client_credentials flow).

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: REST endpoints exist in code (OrdersController: index, create, show) but are completely undocumented. No routes file present, no API documentation, no specification.
findings.gap: No documented API interface. Integration requires source code inspection.
findings.recommendation: Create OpenAPI 3.x specification documenting all endpoints with request/response schemas.

findings.title: No Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: POST /orders creates new order and charges card on every call. No idempotency key support, no deduplication logic.
findings.gap: Duplicate agent calls create duplicate orders and duplicate charges.
findings.recommendation: Add idempotency key support to write endpoints.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: No authentication mechanism of any kind exists. The controller explicitly notes missing auth filters. No OAuth2, no API keys, no mTLS, no service accounts.
findings.gap: Zero authentication. Any caller can invoke any endpoint without identification.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication. Deploy behind API Gateway with authorizer.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. Write operations occur without any record of the caller.
findings.gap: No audit trail. Cannot prove compliance or conduct forensics.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging with principal attribution for all write operations.

findings.title: Sensitive Payment Data Exposed in API Responses
findings.description: System stores payment card data (card_number, card_exp). SELECT * returns all fields including card data to API callers. No field exclusion or access control differentiation.
findings.gap: Agent-facing API responses include sensitive payment card data with no filtering.
findings.recommendation: Exclude card_number and card_exp from API responses. Implement field-level access control.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls for Payment Data
findings.description: Payment card data (PCI-relevant) and customer order data stored on MySQL/EC2 with no data residency controls, no compliance documentation, no region constraints.
findings.gap: No controls preventing cross-region transmission of PCI-relevant data to LLM providers.
findings.recommendation: Document residency requirements. Implement data transmission boundaries for regulated data.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback for Multi-Step Operations
findings.description: Create action saves order then charges card with no transaction wrapper or compensation logic. Partial failures leave inconsistent state.
findings.gap: No rollback or compensation mechanism. Agent-initiated write sequences cannot be undone.
findings.recommendation: Implement transactional wrapper and compensation logic (refund endpoint, order cancellation).

findings.title: No Programmatic API — WebForms Postback Only
findings.description: The application is an ASP.NET WebForms app with no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration requires either direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No programmatic API exists. Agent integration requires UI automation or direct database access — both are brittle and non-auditable.
findings.recommendation: Expose timesheet operations as a REST API with JSON request/response, documented with OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: Non-Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: The btnSave_Click handler performs a raw SQL INSERT with no idempotency key, no duplicate detection, and no unique constraint on business keys.
findings.gap: Write operations are not idempotent. Agent retries or LLM non-determinism will create duplicate timesheet entries.
findings.recommendation: Add unique constraint on (employee_id, entry_date, project) and implement idempotency key support.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses ASP.NET Forms Authentication with session-based cookies only. No support for service accounts, OAuth2 client credentials, API keys, or mTLS.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. Agents cannot authenticate programmatically.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. The btnSave_Click handler writes to the database without logging the authenticated principal, action, or context. No CloudTrail, no application audit log.
findings.gap: Agent actions are completely undetectable and non-attributable. No audit trail exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging with principal attribution for all write operations.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: The application performs single INSERT operations with no transaction management, no saga pattern, no compensation logic, and no undo endpoints.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback for agent-initiated writes. Failed multi-step workflows leave partial state.
findings.recommendation: Implement soft-delete or status-based record management allowing entries to be reversed.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No immutable audit logging is configured for write operations. The SAM template does not define CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs retention policies, or S3 bucket with object lock. The Lambda function does not log write operations with principal attribution. The schema documents this gap for deleteProduct.
findings.gap: Write operations (upsertProduct, deleteProduct) are not logged with authenticated principal attribution in an immutable, tamper-evident store.
findings.recommendation: Add structured audit logging in resolvers capturing principal, operation, target SKU, and timestamp. Configure immutable log storage (CloudWatch Logs with retention + S3 Object Lock, or CloudTrail data events).

findings.title: Write endpoints lack idempotency key support
findings.description: POST /orders, POST /orders/:id/refund, and POST /orders/:id/cancel have no idempotency key support. A duplicate call to refund double-refunds. SAFETY.md documents this as a deliberate gap.
findings.gap: No Idempotency-Key header support, no deduplication logic, no unique constraint enforcement on business keys for write operations.
findings.recommendation: Add Idempotency-Key header support to all state-mutating POST endpoints using middleware that stores keys in PostgreSQL or Redis.

findings.title: No immutable audit logging for write operations
findings.description: No audit logging of authenticated principal for write operations. DELETE /orders/:id performs irreversible hard delete with no audit record. Refund and cancel operations lack principal attribution in logs.
findings.gap: No per-operation audit trail recording authenticated principal, action, and affected resources. No immutable log storage.
findings.recommendation: Add structured audit log emission in each write route handler capturing principal (from JWT), action, resource ID, timestamp. Configure immutable log storage.

findings.title: No data residency governance for customer PII
findings.description: Customer PII stored in PostgreSQL without documented residency requirements or technical controls to prevent cross-border transmission by an agent. Single-region deployment (infra/ecs.yaml) but no enforcement mechanism.
findings.gap: No documented data residency policy. No technical controls restricting data transmission across jurisdictions.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Classify data fields by sensitivity and residency constraints. Implement controls for agent-initiated data handling.

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for multi-step operations
findings.description: Multi-step write operations have no compensation or rollback. The refund method updates order status AND calls payment processor — if payment fails, status is already changed. cancelAndRecallShipment updates status AND recalls dispatch. hardDelete permanently removes data.
findings.gap: No saga pattern, no compensating transactions, no undo endpoints, no soft-delete. Partial state corruption possible on multi-step failures.
findings.recommendation: Wrap multi-step operations in database transactions. Add soft-delete. Implement compensating logic for external call failures.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging — Incomplete Principal Logging and No Tamper-Evidence
findings.description: The create_charge handler logs client_id but refund_charge omits client_id from structured logs. No tamper-evidence configuration exists: no CloudTrail with log file validation, no CloudWatch log retention policy, no log group deletion protection.
findings.gap: Inconsistent principal logging across write operations. No tamper-evidence assurance for audit logs (no CloudTrail, no retention policy, no deletion protection).
findings.recommendation: Add client_id to refund_charge log line. Configure CloudTrail with log file validation. Set CloudWatch log retention policy and deletion protection on log groups.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty — No Residency Controls for Financial Data
findings.description: The payments API stores financial transaction data (charges, refunds, amounts) in DynamoDB without explicit data residency configuration or compliance documentation. No mechanism signals to agent consumers that financial data should not be transmitted cross-region.
findings.gap: No data residency controls, documentation, or classification headers. No region-pinning beyond implicit SAM deployment region.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements. Add residency metadata to API responses. Constrain deployment region explicitly in IaC.

findings.title: Non-Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: Write endpoints use server-generated IDs (uniqid()) with no idempotency key support. Retrying any POST request creates duplicate records.
findings.gap: No idempotency key mechanism exists. No deduplication logic. Retries create duplicates.
findings.recommendation: Add an Idempotency-Key header parameter to write endpoints. Store keys in a deduplication table and return cached responses for duplicate requests.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application only supports session-based username/password authentication. No OAuth2 client credentials, API keys, mTLS, or service account mechanism exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. An agent must use human credentials to authenticate.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key authentication with per-key principal attribution, or OAuth2 client credentials flow.

findings.title: Incomplete and Mutable Audit Logging
findings.description: Only order status changes are logged (in mutable MySQL). User CRUD, return approvals, and inventory changes have no audit trail. Log is stored in same mutable database.
findings.gap: Incomplete audit coverage and mutable log storage. No tamper-evident, immutable audit trail for all write operations.
findings.recommendation: Log all write operations to immutable store (CloudWatch Logs with S3 export and object lock).

findings.title: No Compensation for Multi-Step Workflow
findings.description: Multi-step fulfillment workflow (validate → assign-warehouse → pick → pack → QC → ship) has no compensation logic. Each step is independently committed with no cross-step rollback.
findings.gap: No saga pattern, no compensating transactions, no undo endpoints for multi-step workflow.
findings.recommendation: Implement saga pattern with compensating transactions for each workflow step.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: Single hardcoded database password grants full unrestricted access to all data and operations. No mechanism to scope down access per caller identity.
findings.gap: No scoped permissions. All callers get identical unrestricted access.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based access control with differentiated access levels.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Any caller with the database password can perform any operation on any record without restriction.
findings.gap: Cannot enforce read-only vs. write access per resource type.
findings.recommendation: Implement action-level authorization checks (ABAC or fine-grained RBAC).

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation mechanism exists. Environ("USERNAME") is the only identity source. No JWT, no OAuth token exchange, no on-behalf-of flows.
findings.gap: Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs. agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth 2.0 token exchange when building the API layer.

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials in Source Code
findings.description: Database password hardcoded as a constant: Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw". Connection string embeds this password. No secrets management, no rotation.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code. Exposed in version control history. No rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation. Remove hardcoded credentials from source.

findings.title: No Input Validation — SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: No input validation exists. SQL string concatenation without parameterization creates SQL injection vulnerability. No schema enforcement or structured validation errors.
findings.gap: Arbitrary input accepted without validation. SQL injection risk.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries and request validation with structured error responses.

findings.title: Inadequate Temporal Metadata
findings.description: CreatedOn uses VB6 Now() (local time) with no timezone normalization. No updated_at field. No freshness signaling.
findings.gap: No UTC timestamps, no update tracking, no data freshness indicators.
findings.recommendation: Store timestamps in UTC with timezone metadata. Add updated_at and freshness headers.

findings.title: No PII Redaction Controls
findings.description: No PII redaction controls exist in a system handling customer PII. No logging framework, no structured output, no redaction capabilities.
findings.gap: No PII redaction capability for a system that handles sensitive data.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured logging with PII redaction when modernizing.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning, no API contracts, no migration files, no breaking change detection. Database schema unversioned and undocumented.
findings.gap: No stability guarantees for agent tool schemas.
findings.recommendation: Implement schema versioning, migration tooling, and API contract testing.

findings.title: Zero Test Coverage
findings.description: No tests of any kind exist. README states 'No tests, no build server; compiled on one developer's machine.' Zero automated testing.
findings.gap: No unit, integration, or API tests. No CI pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated API tests and contract tests as part of modernization.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: Access .mdb uses a trivially-bypassable database password (not encryption). No KMS, no disk-level encryption documented.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for customer PII data.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed database with KMS encryption.

findings.title: No Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft or pending state exists. INSERT commits immediately with no reviewable intermediate state, no status field, no two-step commit.
findings.gap: Agent cannot propose changes for human review before finalization.

findings.title: No draft/pending state for agent-proposed writes

findings.title: No distributed tracing or structured logging

findings.title: No alerting on error rates or latency

findings.title: Write-only interface — cannot query current state

findings.title: No circuit breakers or resilience patterns

findings.title: No transaction limits on agent operations

findings.title: No Async Operation Support for Long-Running Batch

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization

findings.title: No Input Validation or Schema Enforcement

findings.title: No Temporal Metadata or Freshness Signals

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning. Fixed-width 120-byte record format is undocumented outside COBOL source. No versioning, no changelog, no breaking-change detection.
findings.gap: No versioning. Format changes break consumers silently.
findings.recommendation: Document record layout formally. Implement schema versioning.

findings.title: Zero Automated Test Coverage

findings.gap: Zero test coverage. No automated validation.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest for data stores containing SSN and bank accounts. No KMS, no encryption config visible.
findings.gap: Sensitive PII stored unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Implement KMS-managed encryption for all data at rest containing PII.

findings.title: No Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft or pending state. Batch job immediately processes and outputs final payroll records with no intermediate review step.
findings.gap: No intermediate reviewable state. All writes immediately committed.
findings.recommendation: Implement two-phase execution with human approval before financial disbursement.

findings.title: No Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No configurable approval gates. JCL job runs both steps automatically with no mechanism to require human approval before high-risk operations.
findings.gap: No operation-level approval configuration.
findings.recommendation: Implement approval gates for financial disbursement and data transmission.

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No dedicated sandbox. Changes validated in shared QA region only — not isolated, not production-equivalent.
findings.gap: No isolated testing environment with production-equivalent data shape.
findings.recommendation: Create sandbox with synthetic payroll data (no real SSNs) for agent testing.

findings.title: No Queryable Current State
findings.description: System does not expose current state in any queryable form. Cannot inspect payroll status or last run before acting.
findings.gap: No state query mechanism. No GET/status APIs.
findings.recommendation: Expose current state (last run, status, record count) via query API.

findings.title: No Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency controls. Concurrent execution produces duplicate payout records. No locking, no version fields, no conditional writes.
findings.gap: No concurrency protection mechanisms.
findings.recommendation: Implement mutual exclusion and idempotency checks.

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers or Resilience Patterns
findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations for the FTP dependency (EC2 gateway at 10.0.7.40). Failure handling is absent.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns for external dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Implement retry with circuit breaker for file transfer step.

findings.title: No Blast Radius or Transaction Limits
findings.description: No transaction limits. Batch processes ALL employees with no configurable caps on records or disbursement amounts.
findings.gap: No blast radius limits. No per-run caps.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable limits on records processed and total disbursement amount.

findings.title: No Graceful Degradation Signaling
findings.description: No degradation signaling. No health endpoints, no freshness indicators, no machine-readable status signals.
findings.gap: No degradation signaling mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Implement health/status endpoints with data freshness.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or any machine-readable specification exists. API behavior defined only in C++ source code.
findings.gap: No machine-readable spec. Agent tool generation requires manual reverse-engineering.
findings.recommendation: Create OpenAPI 3.0 specification after implementing JSON response (API-Q1).

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: All responses return HTTP 200 with HTML. Unknown SKU returns $0.00 instead of 404. Invalid quantity silently treated as 0. No error codes or retryable indication.
findings.gap: No structured errors. Agent cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement HTTP status codes (404, 400) and structured error bodies with error code, message, and retryable flag.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions Model
findings.description: No authorization model exists. All callers have identical unrestricted access with no mechanism to differentiate access levels.
findings.gap: Cannot scope agent permissions. No role-based or attribute-based access control.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway usage plans with scoped API keys or OAuth2 scopes after establishing machine identity.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No authorization logic exists at any level. Cannot enforce action-level access control per caller.
findings.gap: No action-level authorization. No mechanism to enforce read-only access for agents.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level authorization at the API Gateway layer, restricting agent identities to GET operations only.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No application-level audit logging exists. Apache access logs are ephemeral, not immutable, not shipped to central log store, and lack principal attribution.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail for agent actions. Cannot determine which agent made a request.
findings.recommendation: Configure API Gateway access logging to CloudWatch with retention and S3 archival for immutability.

findings.title: No Input Validation — Buffer Overflow and XSS Vulnerabilities
findings.description: Zero input validation. strcpy on attacker-controlled query strings without bounds checking (buffer overflow). SKU echoed to HTML without escaping (XSS). No range checking on qty.
findings.gap: No validation, known buffer overflow and XSS vulnerabilities. No structured rejection for malformed input.
findings.recommendation: Replace unsafe C string functions with bounded alternatives, add input length limits, validate SKU format, validate qty range, return structured 400 errors.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning, no API contracts, no changelog, no version prefix in URL, no breaking change detection, no consumer-driven contract tests.
findings.gap: No API stability guarantees. Changes to CGI response format would silently break agent bindings.
findings.recommendation: Define versioned API contract (OpenAPI spec) with semantic versioning and version prefix.

findings.title: Partial Infrastructure Governance — No Review or Drift Detection
findings.description: K8s manifests exist (IaC present) but lack change review enforcement and drift detection. Only 1 of 3 sub-checks satisfied (IaC defined, but no peer review enforcement and no drift detection).
findings.gap: IaC exists but governance incomplete. No CODEOWNERS, no branch protection, no drift reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Adopt GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux) for K8s manifest deployment with PR-based review and drift reconciliation.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild. Legacy deployment was scp. Containerized path has no automation.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy pipeline. API-breaking changes not caught before production.
findings.recommendation: Create CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodeBuild) with Docker build, integration tests, and ECR push.

findings.title: No Automated Rollback Capability
findings.description: No explicit rollback mechanism configured. K8s supports native rollout undo but no automated triggers, canary deployment, or blue/green strategy defined.
findings.gap: No automated rollback. Recovery depends on manual kubectl rollout undo.
findings.recommendation: Add automated rollback with Argo Rollouts or Flagger canary analysis.

findings.title: No Sandbox or Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment defined. Single K8s namespace with no environment differentiation. No docker-compose for local development.
findings.gap: No safe environment for agent testing. First agent interaction would be in production.
findings.recommendation: Create docker-compose.yaml for local agent testing and add staging K8s namespace with Kustomize overlays.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or structured logging. CGI produces only stdout HTML. Apache access logs are unstructured with no correlation IDs or trace propagation.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests not debuggable. No tracing, no correlation IDs.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry at API Gateway/ingress layer. Configure Apache JSON access logs with X-Request-Id.

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring dashboards, no anomaly detection. Only K8s liveness/readiness probes exist.
findings.gap: No alerting. Target system degradation affecting agents goes undetected.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch Container Insights for EKS, add alarms on HTTP 5xx rate and p99 latency.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting or Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting exists at any layer. Apache httpd serves requests without throttling. No API Gateway, WAF rules, or application-level rate limiting. A runaway agent loop could overwhelm the service.
findings.gap: No per-caller rate limiting. K8s resource limits provide a hard ceiling but do not reject excess requests gracefully.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway or ingress controller with throttling (e.g., 100 req/s per API key).

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or Smithy specification exists in the repository. The API surface (GET /rates, POST /quote) is defined only in server.js code.
findings.gap: Agent frameworks cannot auto-generate tool definitions. Every integration requires manual tool authoring.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification documenting the two endpoints, their parameters, and response schemas.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses are minimal JSON objects with only a message string: { error: 'invalid api key' }, { error: 'db error' }, { error: 'query error' }. No error codes, no retryable indicator, no consistent error schema.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable errors from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured error responses with error code, message, and retryable boolean.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: The application has a single shared API key that grants identical access to all endpoints (GET /rates, POST /quote) for all callers. No mechanism exists to scope down permissions per caller.
findings.gap: No authorization model supporting scoped permissions. All callers get the same broad access.
findings.recommendation: Introduce API Gateway with resource-level policies or implement RBAC middleware in the application.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The API key middleware grants blanket access to all operations. There is no distinction between read and write permissions.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read-only access (GET /rates) while denying POST /quote access.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level authorization, either at API Gateway or application middleware layer.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: The API key is hardcoded in source code: var API_KEY = 'ship-2013-abc123-static'. The MongoDB connection URL is also hardcoded: var MONGO_URL = 'mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping'. While the K8s deployment externalizes these via Secret and ConfigMap, the hardcoded values persist in the source repository.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code are exposed to anyone with repository access and persist in git history. No secrets management system with rotation.
findings.recommendation: Remove all hardcoded credentials from server.js. Read API_KEY and MONGO_URL exclusively from environment variables. Integrate AWS Secrets Manager for credential storage and rotation.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. The application has no structured logging of authenticated principals, no request logging, and no immutable log storage configuration. The only logging is console.log('Shipping API listening on 8080').
findings.gap: No audit trail for any API call. Cannot determine who called what endpoint or when.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured request logging with caller identity. Deploy CloudTrail or CloudWatch Logs with immutable retention.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No mechanism to suspend or revoke individual agent identities. The single shared API key means suspending one caller requires changing the key for all callers, causing a service disruption.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without affecting all API consumers.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to per-agent API keys via API Gateway with ability to disable individual keys, or implement OAuth2 client credentials with token revocation.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: GET /rates returns all matching documents from MongoDB via .find(filter).toArray() with no pagination, no limit parameter, no cursor-based pagination, and no result size cap.
findings.gap: An agent querying rates for a broad origin/destination pair could receive an unbounded result set.
findings.recommendation: Add limit and offset (or cursor) query parameters to GET /rates. Enforce a maximum result size.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation exists. GET /rates passes req.query.origin and req.query.dest directly into the MongoDB filter with no sanitization — a potential NoSQL injection vector. POST /quote uses req.body.weight and req.body.zone in arithmetic with no type checking.
findings.gap: Malformed agent inputs are not rejected. The system accepts arbitrary query shapes without validation.
findings.recommendation: Add input validation (joi or express-validator) for all endpoints. Sanitize MongoDB query inputs. Return structured validation errors.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal metadata in API responses. MongoDB documents returned as-is with no timestamps indicating when rates were last updated. No Cache-Control or freshness headers.
findings.gap: Agent cannot determine whether shipping rates are current or stale.
findings.recommendation: Add updated_at timestamp fields to rate documents. Include Cache-Control or X-Data-Age response headers.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No API versioning (no /v1/ prefix, no Accept-Version header). No schema files, no changelog, no contract tests, no migration files.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings break silently when API changes are deployed.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL-based API versioning (/v1/rates, /v1/quote). Add OpenAPI diff checks to CI.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests exist (deployment.yaml, service.yaml, configmap.yaml, namespace.yaml) providing partial IaC. No PR/review requirements configured, no drift detection active.
findings.gap: IaC partially defines deployment surface but lacks peer review enforcement and drift detection. No API Gateway or IAM definitions.
findings.recommendation: Implement GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux) for K8s manifest deployment with PR-based review. Add API Gateway and IAM definitions to IaC.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml found.
findings.gap: API contract changes cannot be caught before agents are affected.
findings.recommendation: Establish a CI/CD pipeline with automated API contract tests using the OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Kubernetes Deployment provides native rollback capability via kubectl rollout undo. However, no automated rollback triggers, no blue/green deployment, no canary strategy.
findings.gap: Rollback is available but entirely manual. No health-based automatic rollback.
findings.recommendation: Configure deployment strategy with automatic rollback triggers (Argo Rollouts or CodeDeploy).

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: No test files exist in the repository. No test framework in dependencies. No test directory.
findings.gap: Zero automated test coverage for agent-facing APIs.
findings.recommendation: Add API integration tests using supertest/jest validating GET /rates and POST /quote.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No encryption at rest configuration for the MongoDB data store. The MongoDB connection string uses no TLS options. No KMS key references.
findings.gap: Data at rest in MongoDB is not demonstrably encrypted.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a managed database service (DocumentDB or MongoDB Atlas) with encryption at rest enabled.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration exists. No docker-compose for local testing, no seed data scripts, no multi-environment K8s overlays.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior against production-equivalent data.
findings.recommendation: Create a docker-compose.yml for local development with MongoDB container and seed data. Add K8s overlays for staging.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing (no X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry SDK). No structured logging — the only log statement is console.log('Shipping API listening on 8080'). No correlation IDs, no JSON logging.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated request failures are completely undebuggable.
findings.recommendation: Add structured JSON logging with request_id correlation. Integrate AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry SDK.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration.
findings.gap: Target system degradation affecting agents will not be detected until cascading failures occur.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for 5xx error rate and p99 latency.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanism exists for any operation. The application has no transaction management, no saga patterns, and no undo endpoints.
findings.gap: If agent scope expands to write-enabled, there is no mechanism to reverse or compensate failed multi-step operations.
findings.recommendation: Before expanding to write-enabled agent scope, implement compensation logic or two-phase commit patterns for any write operations.

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: The application connects to MongoDB on every request with no connection pooling, no retry logic, no timeout configuration, and no circuit breaker pattern. A MongoDB outage causes all requests to hang or fail with generic 500 errors.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns for the external MongoDB dependency. Agent traffic during a MongoDB outage accumulates pending connections.
findings.recommendation: Implement MongoDB connection pooling, connection timeouts, and circuit breaker logic. Add exponential backoff for retries.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting exists at any layer. No API Gateway throttling, no WAF rules, no application-level rate limiting middleware. The K8s service is exposed as ClusterIP with no ingress rate controls.
findings.gap: A runaway agent loop can overwhelm the service at machine speed. Each request opens a new MongoDB connection, amplifying the impact.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with throttling configuration (requests/second per key). Alternatively, add express-rate-limit middleware.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or Smithy specification exists. No machine-readable API specification of any kind.
findings.gap: Agent frameworks cannot auto-generate tool definitions. Every integration requires manual tool authoring.
findings.recommendation: Create OpenAPI 3.x specification for the three endpoints.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Controller renders HTML on failure. No structured JSON error responses, no error codes, no retryable indicators.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable errors from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON error responses with error code, message, and retryable boolean.

findings.title: No Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: Payment processing executes synchronously within the HTTP request. No background job framework, no async patterns, no polling endpoints.
findings.gap: Long-running payment calls may timeout agent requests.
findings.recommendation: Implement async payment processing with a job queue and status polling endpoint.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: No authorization model exists. No IAM policies, no RBAC, no permission scoping mechanism.
findings.gap: Cannot scope agent permissions to specific resources or operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC or deploy behind API Gateway with scoped IAM roles.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization. No ABAC, no fine-grained RBAC, no permission matrices.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict agents to specific operations within a resource type.
findings.recommendation: Implement action-level before_filter authorization.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation mechanism. No JWT parsing, no OAuth token exchange, no on-behalf-of flows.
findings.gap: Cannot distinguish agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement JWT-based identity propagation with distinct flows.

findings.title: Credentials Hardcoded in Source Control
findings.description: Payment gateway credentials (merchant_id, api_password) hardcoded in config/payment.yml in plaintext, checked into source control.
findings.gap: Credentials exposed in source control. No secrets management, no rotation.
findings.recommendation: Rotate credentials immediately. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Capability
findings.description: No identity management system. Cannot issue, track, or revoke agent identities.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without taking down the application.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key management with per-agent keys and individual revocation.

findings.title: No Pagination on Query Endpoints
findings.description: GET /orders has status filter but no pagination (no limit, offset, cursor). Returns all matching orders unbounded.
findings.gap: Unbounded result sets exhaust LLM context windows.
findings.recommendation: Implement cursor-based pagination with configurable page size.

findings.title: No Input Validation — SQL Injection and Mass Assignment
findings.description: No input validation. SQL injection via string interpolation in find_by_sql. Mass assignment vulnerability via unfiltered params[:order].
findings.gap: Malformed/malicious inputs accepted without rejection. Data corruption and injection possible.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries. Add attr_accessible. Implement structured validation error responses.

findings.title: Minimal Temporal Metadata, No Freshness Signaling
findings.description: created_at field exists in schema. No updated_at visible, no timezone normalization documented, no Cache-Control or freshness headers.
findings.gap: Agents cannot assess data freshness or staleness.
findings.recommendation: Ensure created_at/updated_at with UTC. Add Cache-Control and Last-Modified headers.

findings.title: No PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: No PII redaction. Application processes credit card numbers (card_number, card_exp) with no log filtering or masking.
findings.gap: PCI data likely appears in Rails default parameter logs.
findings.recommendation: Configure Rails filter_parameters for card_number, card_exp, api_password.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No API versioning, no changelog, no breaking change detection, no contract tests.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings would break silently on any API change.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-based API versioning and breaking change detection.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC. Capistrano 2 deployment to fixed EC2 hosts. No Terraform, CloudFormation, or CDK.
findings.gap: No IaC definition, no change review, no drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure as code starting with API-facing surface.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline of any kind. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline to catch API-breaking changes.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with API contract testing.

findings.title: Unvalidated Rollback Capability
findings.description: Capistrano 2 has theoretical rollback but not validated. No blue/green, canary, or feature flags.
findings.gap: No modern deployment safety patterns.
findings.recommendation: Validate Capistrano rollback. Migrate to modern deployment strategy.

findings.title: No Working API Test Coverage
findings.description: Tests are stale and no longer run. Zero working automated test coverage for API endpoints.
findings.gap: Behavior changes cannot be validated automatically.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials in Configuration

findings.gap: Credentials exposed in version control. Prompt injection or agent bug could leak them.

findings.title: No Pagination or Filtering

findings.gap: Unbounded result sets exhaust agent context windows.

findings.gap: No validation at any layer. Malformed input corrupts data or enables injection.

findings.title: No Temporal Metadata or Freshness Signaling
findings.description: Only entry_date exists. No created_at/updated_at, no timezone handling, no freshness indicators.
findings.gap: Cannot determine data freshness or temporal context.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts

findings.recommendation: Implement configurable approval gates by operation type.

findings.description: No staging environment. Single production server with manual deployment.

findings.title: No Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs anywhere in the application.

findings.title: No Alerting Configuration
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring, no health checks. No observability stack.

findings.gap: Agents cannot inspect current state before acting.
findings.recommendation: Expose GET endpoint returning timesheet entries as JSON.

findings.description: No optimistic locking, no version fields, no conditional writes. Concurrent agents can insert conflicting records.
findings.gap: No protection against race conditions from concurrent agent instances.
findings.recommendation: Implement optimistic locking or unique constraints on business keys.

findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations. Raw SqlConnection with no error handling.
findings.gap: Database failures cascade directly to agents as unstructured errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement circuit breaker pattern and connection timeouts.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level throttling.
findings.gap: Runaway agent loop can overwhelm the application at machine speed.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway or proxy with per-caller rate limiting.

findings.title: No Transaction Limits (Unbounded Blast Radius)
findings.description: No configurable limits on agent-initiated actions. Unlimited writes per session with no caps.
findings.gap: Agent error blast radius is unbounded — could create thousands of bogus records.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller business transaction limits.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Apollo Server returns structured GraphQL errors but the requireScope function throws a generic new Error('forbidden: ...') resulting in extensions.code: INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR for permission errors. No retryable indicator exists in error responses.
findings.gap: Error codes are inconsistent (permission errors appear as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) and have no retryable indicator.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: The system extracts JWT claims from API Gateway authorizer context and uses scopes for authorization. However, there is no mechanism to distinguish between an agent acting under its own service identity vs. acting on behalf of a specific human user. No token exchange or on-behalf-of flow is implemented.
findings.gap: Cannot differentiate agent-as-self calls from agent-on-behalf-of-user calls. All authenticated callers are treated identically based on scopes alone.
findings.recommendation: Implement distinct authentication flows for agent-as-self (client_credentials) and agent-on-behalf-of-user (authorization_code with token exchange), and enforce different permission boundaries for each mode.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Products have an updatedAt field set to ISO 8601 UTC timestamp on every write. However, there is no createdAt timestamp, and the products query uses DynamoDB scan which is eventually consistent by default with no freshness signaling to the caller.
findings.gap: No creation timestamp. No data freshness signaling for eventually-consistent scan results.
findings.recommendation: Add createdAt timestamp on initial creation and document/signal data consistency level in responses.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: The GraphQL schema (schema/catalog.graphql) is well-documented but has no versioning scheme. No version identifier, no changelog, no breaking change detection tooling, no consumer-driven contract tests.
findings.gap: Schema changes could break agent tool bindings silently with no detection mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Add schema versioning and integrate breaking change detection (e.g., graphql-inspector diff) in CI.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Infrastructure is defined as SAM/CloudFormation (infra/template.yaml). However, no evidence of peer review requirements (no CODEOWNERS file) or drift detection (no AWS Config rules).
findings.gap: IaC exists (sub-check 1 passes) but change review enforcement and drift detection are not evidenced.
findings.recommendation: Add CODEOWNERS with mandatory review for infra/ and enable CloudFormation drift detection.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration exists in the repository. No .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, or any pipeline definition was found.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline to test, validate, or deploy the service. No mechanism to catch API-breaking changes before production.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodePipeline + CodeBuild) that runs tsc, vitest, and GraphQL schema validation.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No deployment automation or rollback mechanism is configured. No blue/green, no canary, no Lambda alias traffic shifting, no CodeDeploy configuration.
findings.gap: A broken deployment cannot be automatically rolled back.
findings.recommendation: Add DeploymentPreference with Canary10Percent5Minutes and alarm-triggered rollback to the SAM function.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: The vitest test framework is configured as a devDependency and a test script exists in package.json. However, no test files (.test.ts, .spec.ts) were found in the repository.
findings.gap: Zero test coverage for the GraphQL API.
findings.recommendation: Create tests covering valid queries, mutation authorization, idempotency behavior, pagination, and error responses.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: All mutations commit immediately. upsertProduct writes directly to DynamoDB with active: true. deleteProduct immediately sets active=false. No draft, pending, or proposed state exists in the data model.
findings.gap: An agent cannot propose a change for human review before it takes effect. All writes are immediately committed.
findings.recommendation: Extend the Product schema with a status field supporting DRAFT/PENDING states, and add a confirmProduct mutation that transitions from PENDING to ACTIVE.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval workflow exists. Mutations execute immediately without any configurable approval step. No Step Functions with human approval tasks.
findings.gap: High-risk operations cannot be gated behind human approval at the application layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement configurable approval gates for mutation types that exceed risk thresholds.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No separate environment configurations, no docker-compose for local testing, no seed data scripts, no staging-specific SAM configuration.
findings.gap: No sandbox or staging environment for testing agent behavior with production-equivalent data shape.
findings.recommendation: Add samconfig.toml with staging and production environments, and create a seed data script.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: X-Ray tracing is active (Tracing: Active in SAM template Globals). However, no structured logging library is configured — no JSON logger, no correlation_id field, no request_id propagation in application logs.
findings.gap: Tracing exists but structured logging with correlation IDs is absent. Cannot correlate application logs with specific agent-initiated requests.
findings.recommendation: Add @aws-lambda-powertools/logger with structured JSON output and inject API Gateway request ID as correlation ID.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms are defined in the SAM template. No anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration, no SLO-based alerting configured.
findings.gap: API degradation or elevated error rates will not be detected automatically.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for Lambda errors (>1% error rate), p99 latency (>5s), and throttles.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: Both mutations use unconditional DynamoDB writes. upsertProduct uses PutItem without a condition expression (last-writer-wins). deleteProduct uses UpdateExpression without a condition. No version field, no optimistic locking, no ETag support.
findings.gap: Concurrent agent instances writing to the same SKU will silently overwrite each other's changes with no conflict detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a version attribute and use DynamoDB conditional writes (ConditionExpression: version = :expected) to detect concurrent modifications.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No explicit rate limiting is configured in the SAM template. The HTTP API has no ThrottlingBurstLimit or ThrottlingRateLimit properties. No WAF rules are defined. API Gateway HTTP API default account-level throttle (10,000 rps) is too high to protect against agent loops.
findings.gap: A runaway agent loop could execute thousands of mutations per second with no service-level protection.
findings.recommendation: Configure explicit throttling on the HTTP API route (ThrottlingBurstLimit, ThrottlingRateLimit) in infra/template.yaml and consider per-client throttling via WAF.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No per-agent transaction limits are configured. While mutations operate on single records (one SKU per call), there is no mechanism to cap total operations per agent identity per time window.
findings.gap: No configurable business transaction limits (e.g., max mutations per hour per caller identity).
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller mutation rate tracking that rejects requests exceeding configurable thresholds.

findings.title: Error responses lack retryable indicator
findings.description: Error responses use consistent {code, message} format but lack a retryable boolean or error category for agent self-correction.
findings.gap: No retryable boolean or error category in error responses.
findings.recommendation: Add retryable field to error response schema.

findings.title: No async pattern for external service calls
findings.description: Refund and cancel operations call external services synchronously. No background job framework or polling endpoints.
findings.gap: No async operation support for potentially long-running external calls.

findings.title: No identity propagation to downstream services

findings.gap: No identity propagation to downstream services. No mechanism to distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement token exchange or pass-through of caller JWT claims to downstream service calls.

findings.title: No immediate agent identity suspension mechanism
findings.description: JWT-based auth relies on token expiry for revocation. No token deny-list or immediate suspension mechanism in the application.
findings.gap: No in-application token deny-list. Immediate revocation depends entirely on external IdP.
findings.recommendation: Add a token deny-list cache (Redis-backed) checked on each request, or implement jti claim validation against a revocation store.

findings.title: No input validation at API boundary
findings.description: No input validation library used. Route handlers cast request bodies with TypeScript type assertions without runtime validation.
findings.gap: No systematic input validation. Malformed payloads accepted without structured rejection.
findings.recommendation: Add Fastify schema validation using built-in ajv support. Define request body schemas for write endpoints.

findings.title: No temporal metadata on order records
findings.description: Order interface has no created_at, updated_at, or event_time fields. No data freshness indicators in API responses.
findings.gap: No timestamp fields. Agents cannot determine data freshness.

findings.title: No PII redaction in application logs
findings.description: Service handles customer PII. README documents structured logging (pino) but no PII redaction mechanism visible. No log scrubbing middleware or masking library.
findings.gap: No PII redaction. Customer data may be logged unmasked.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline with API contract testing

findings.gap: No test files despite framework being configured.

findings.description: All write operations immediately committed. Order status enum (placed, shipped, cancelled, refunded) has no PENDING or DRAFT state. Agent-initiated refund or cancellation executes immediately.
findings.gap: No draft/pending state mechanism. All writes are final on execution.

findings.description: Structured logging claimed (pino with request_id) and CloudWatch Logs configured, but no distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry/X-Ray). Cannot trace requests through downstream services.

findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms defined. No alerting for error rates, latency, or anomaly detection.
findings.gap: API degradation affecting agents would go undetected.

findings.description: No optimistic or pessimistic locking. Multiple concurrent agent instances could issue conflicting updates. No version fields, ETags, or SELECT FOR UPDATE patterns.

findings.title: No rate limiting on API endpoints

findings.title: Schema Versioning — No Breaking-Change Detection
findings.description: OpenAPI spec is versioned (1.4.0) with URL path versioning (/v1/). Spec validated in CI. No breaking-change detection tooling (no OpenAPI diff, no Pact).
findings.gap: No automated breaking-change detection in CI.
findings.recommendation: Add oasdiff breaking-change detection to CI pipeline.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance — No Peer Review or Drift Detection
findings.description: IaC present (SAM template). CI runs on push and pull_request. No explicit branch protection rules, required reviewers, or drift detection configuration.
findings.gap: No mandatory peer review for IaC changes. No drift detection.

findings.title: CI/CD Contract Testing — No Breaking-Change Detection
findings.description: CI validates OpenAPI spec structure and runs pytest. No consumer-driven contract tests (Pact) and no breaking-change detection comparing spec against previous versions.
findings.gap: No API-breaking-change detection. No consumer contract testing.

findings.recommendation: Implement optional pending state for agent-initiated charges with a confirm endpoint.

findings.title: Approval Gates — No Configurable Human Approval
findings.description: All operations execute immediately upon authentication and scope verification. No mechanism to require human approval for high-value charges or bulk refunds.
findings.gap: No operation-level approval configuration. No threshold-based gates.

findings.description: Tests run against DynamoDB Local stubs. No staging/sandbox environment configuration in IaC. Single-environment SAM template.

findings.title: Blast Radius — No Transaction Limits
findings.description: No configurable business-domain transaction limits exist. An agent could issue unlimited refunds or create unlimited charges per hour without any system-enforced cap.
findings.gap: No per-caller transaction limits (max_refunds_per_hour, max_charge_amount_per_session).

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification

findings.title: Unstructured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses return {"error": "<message>"} with HTTP status codes but no error codes, retryable flag, or category classification.

findings.title: No Asynchronous Operation Support

findings.title: Coarse-Grained Permissions

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level checks within the admin role. All operations (read, write, delete) are permitted equally once admin is authenticated.

findings.recommendation: Add action-level permission checks (canRead, canWrite, canDelete) per endpoint.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation or Delegation
findings.description: No JWT, OAuth2 on-behalf-of, or token exchange patterns. Session-based auth cannot distinguish agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-user.

findings.recommendation: Implement JWT with actor/subject claims for identity propagation.

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials Without Secrets Management
findings.description: Database credentials have hardcoded fallback defaults in source code. Seed data includes hardcoded plaintext passwords. No secrets management system (Secrets Manager, Vault) is used.

findings.recommendation: Integrate AWS Secrets Manager for database credentials with automatic rotation. Remove all hardcoded defaults.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Mechanism

findings.title: No Access Control Differentiation for Sensitive Data

findings.title: No Pagination or Filtering on List Endpoints

findings.title: Minimal Input Validation Without Structured Errors

findings.title: Timestamps Without Timezone Normalization or Freshness Signaling

findings.title: No PII Redaction in Logs or Error Responses

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
